questions.stem: GridCap's service moves to a workstation with a GPU. Under the lesson's policy, which job stays on the CPU whatever the machine has?

options.text: The final capital plan, which an auditor must be able to repeat
options.says: Right: the plan of record runs on HiGHS with one thread on every machine, because it must repeat bit for bit.

options.text: The large LP bound, which a GPU solves within its tolerance
options.says: With a GPU, the 300 x 300 LP bound goes to HiGHS's GPU PDLP and is verified on the CPU.

options.text: The starting plan for tonight's run, checked before it is used
options.says: With a GPU, the starting plan goes to cuOpt and is checked; it changes device.

options.text: None of them: once a GPU is present, every job moves to it
options.says: Three of the five jobs keep the same CPU policy with or without a GPU.

origin.section: One Object Decides the Device, Solver, Method, Threads and Tolerance

questions.stem: Under the policy, a large LP is sent to HiGHS's GPU PDLP, which returns Unknown, so the run falls back to the CPU. What does the manifest's policy block hold?

options.text: The GPU policy, since it was the one decided first
options.says: run asks the policy again without a GPU, and the record holds the policy that actually ran.

options.text: The GPU policy with only its device field set to cpu
options.says: The CPU branch has its own method and tolerance (interior point at 1e-8); a patched GPU block would record a run that never happened.

options.text: No policy at all, since the fallback broke the policy
options.says: The fallback is part of the policy: every GPU branch has a CPU branch, and that one is recorded.

options.text: The CPU policy that decide returns when there is no GPU
options.says: Right: run calls decide(job, gpu=False) and records that policy, so the manifest says what ran.

origin.section: The Policy Falls Back to the CPU and Is Recorded in the Manifest

questions.stem: Tonight's cuOpt plan passed every check and is worth 0.01% more than last night's HiGHS plan. An analyst wants to sign the cuOpt plan as the capital plan. What does the policy allow?

options.text: Give it to HiGHS as a start, and sign the plan HiGHS returns
options.says: Right: a checked GPU plan is a start; the signed plan comes from the CPU run that repeats.

options.text: Sign it, since it passed the rows, integrality and gap checks
options.says: Passing the checks makes it a usable start, not the plan of record, which never comes from the GPU.

options.text: Sign it if a second cuOpt run returns the very same plan
options.says: A matching second run is luck, not a promise: cuOpt's MILP plans do not repeat.

options.text: Discard it, since a GPU plan has no use for a capital plan
options.says: A GPU answer may serve as a bound or a start, each verified on the CPU.

origin.section: A GPU Result Serves a Capital Plan Only as a Bound or a Start, Verified on the CPU
